title: Sales enablement playbook — positioning, competitive briefs, pitch decks, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook is the canonical sales enablement guide for Redwood Inference for field reps, SDRs, SEs, and customer-facing product marketing. It consolidates messaging, competitive positioning, standard pitch deck structure, pricing guidance, reproducible case studies, objection-handling, and a prospect-facing Security FAQ. Use this document as the source of truth for demo narratives, pricing examples, and competitive calls.

Audience
- Field sales (AE, SE)
- Solutions Engineers and Sales Enablement
- Product Marketing and GTM leaders
- Customer Success for handoffs and expansions

Executive summary (elevator pitches)
- 15s: "Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that gives teams predictable latency, lower per-token cost, and unified operations across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- 30s: "We help engineering teams ship LLM features with production-grade performance and predictable economics — whether on our hosted API, reserved Dedicated capacity, or Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments. Customers reduce latency variability, cut per-token costs through batching and cache, and gain operational control with rollout and observability tools."

Positioning & messaging framework
- Primary value props (ranked):
  1) Predictable production economics: reduce per-token cost and variance with smart batching, caching, and routing.
  2) Production SLAs + reliability: canary rollouts, A/B model routing, transparent fallbacks.
  3) Deployment flexibility: same API and controls across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
  4) Developer velocity: quick SDKs, streaming, function/tool calling, and built-in evals.
  5) Observability & cost transparency: token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards.

- Messaging by persona:
  - Engineering/ML Engineers: emphasize runtime performance, model catalog, kernel-level optimizations, quantization profiles, and local private deployment options.
  - Platform/Infra: emphasize predictable capacity (Dedicated), network isolation (VPC), and KMS/HSM integrations.
  - Product/PM: emphasize developer productivity (SDKs, quickstarts), rollout controls, and eval-driven quality guards.
  - Procurement/Finance: emphasize unit economics, reserved capacity discounts, and clear billing models.

Competitor brief (one-page summary)
- Competitor categories: 1) Cloud AI platforms (managed endpoints from cloud providers), 2) LLM API aggregators/providers, 3) Inference orchestration vendors/self-hosted runtimes.

- Generic competitive table (use in one-pager):
  | Competitor | Strengths | Typical customer | How we win | Key rebuttal points |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Cloud AI (C1, C2) | Integrated cloud services, large infra footprint | Enterprises already on their cloud | We win on developer experience, observability, lower latency variance, and flexible private deployments | They have scale; emphasize vendor lock-in and less inference-optimized runtimes |
  | LLM API providers (P1, P2) | Simple APIs, curated models | Startups and apps needing fast time-to-value | We win on cost controls, dedicated capacity, privacy options | They’re simpler; emphasize high transaction costs at scale |
  | Inference infra vendors (I1, I2) | Deep control for self-hosters | Platform teams with ops resources | We win with a unified product (hosted + dedicated + private) and less operational burden | They offer more control; emphasize our performance-verified model profiles and SLAs |

- Recommended framing per competitor type:
  - Against cloud provider endpoints: contrast latency variability and per-token economics; show a benchmark slide with tail latency and cost per million tokens.
  - Against API providers: emphasize long-term TCO and Private options (VPC/on‑prem) for regulated customers.
  - Against infra vendors: emphasize managed ops, model catalog, and rapid onboarding plus hybrid deployment options.

Pitch deck standard outline (10–12 slides recommended)
1) Title + intro (logo, tagline, one-line value)
2) Customer problem statement (latency variability, cost unpredictability, deployment lock-in, compliance)
3) Why now (model & infra fragmentation; need for serving-first platform)
4) Product overview (hosted API, Dedicated, Private)
5) Technical differentiators (runtime, batching, routing, quantization)
6) Observability & operator experience (console screenshots: token costs, per-route metrics)
7) Pricing and commercial models (high-level tiers & examples)
8) Case studies / customer outcomes (metrics)
9) Security & compliance (KMS, audit logs, SOC/ISO attachments)
10) Roadmap and SLAs (availability, latency targets)
11) Next steps & asks (POC options, pilot contract template, timeline)
12) Appendix: benchmarks, API examples, model catalog

Demo checklist (pre-demo prep)
- Confirm the prospect’s primary persona, workloads (chat, embeddings, rerank), expected qps, average sequence length, PII/regulatory constraints, and desired region.
- Choose demo model variant aligned with prospect’s latency/cost needs (e.g., quantized variant for cost-sensitive, full-precision for accuracy-sensitive).
- Prepare a live probe: sample request that demonstrates streaming + function calling + fallback.
- Bring cost example: show token breakdown and billing simulation for a representative monthly volume.
- Runbook: if showing Dedicated/Private, have an ops slide summarizing expected lead times (Dedicated: 2–4 weeks for reserved pools; Private VPC: 4–8 weeks depending on network setup).

Pricing guidance & examples
- Pricing models:
  - Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token generation and per-embedding units; ideal for pilots and early-stage apps.
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual commit for guaranteed throughput; includes capacity discounts and priority routing.
  - Private (enterprise license + support): fixed platform fee + possible per-instance compute charge; includes audit/compliance add-ons.

- Discounting and packaging rules (field playbook):
  - Standard starter package: 3-month pilot on Hosted with $X in credits and a follow-up Dedicated proposal if 90-day avg QPS > threshold.
  - Committed Dedicated discounts: 10% for 6-month, 20% for 12-month, and tiered volume discounts beyond committed GPU-hours.
  - Enterprise licensing: negotiation zone — require Legal + RevOps + Sales Eng involvement for any >25% discount off list.

- Pricing example (representative calculation):
  - Use case: consumer chat app, 100M tokens/month (generation+prompt), average latency requirement <250ms, mixed precision OK.
  - Hosted estimate: $0.0008 per generation token (example list price) -> 100M tokens = $80,000 / month.
  - Dedicated estimate: reserved pool pricing reduces per-token compute delta by ~40% at scale (net estimate: ~$48,000 / month) + reserved monthly fee $8,000.
  - Notes: examples are illustrative and must be replaced with current rate card from Pricing team before quoting.

Case studies (repeatable templates for sales decks)
- Template structure: Customer challenge -> Approach (Redwood deployment mode) -> Implementation (timelines, max qps, integration notes) -> Outcomes (quantified metrics) -> Quote & next steps.

- Case study A: AI-native startup (FinTech chatbot)
  - Challenge: needed sub-200ms median latency, pricing predictability, and rapid scaling for a product-led growth motion.
  - Approach: Hosted API initially, migrated to Dedicated after 3 months commit due to traffic patterns.
  - Implementation: 6-week migration; used quantized model variant + prefix KV caching.
  - Outcomes: median latency reduced from 320ms -> 170ms; per-token cost reduced by 38%; uptime 99.98% over 6 months.
  - Customer quote: "Redwood made our chat product reliable at scale while cutting cloud spend."

- Case study B: Regulated enterprise (Healthcare analytics vendor)
  - Challenge: data residency, auditability, and encryption at rest/transport.
  - Approach: Private deployment (VPC) with KMS integration and audit logging.
  - Implementation: 10-week deployment with network validation and compliance attestation.
  - Outcomes: passed internal SOC-like audit; reduced inference latency variability by 25% vs prior self-hosted solution; enabling new HIPAA workloads.

Objection handling (common scenarios)
- "Cloud provider endpoints are cheaper": Ask about tail latency, model variants, and the total cost of ownership including ops. Provide benchmark and quant economics.
- "We’re worried about vendor lock-in": Emphasize model/version pinning, ability to run Private deployments, and exportable prompts/evals.
- "We need on-prem for compliance": Present Private deployment playbook and estimated timelines; show prior customer templates.

Security FAQ for prospects (prospect-facing, short answers)
Q: Where are customer requests processed?
A: Hosted requests are processed in the region selected by the customer; Dedicated pools can be region- or zone-scoped; Private deployments run in customer-managed networks (VPC or on-prem).

Q: How do you protect data in transit and at rest?
A: TLS 1.2+/mTLS for in-transit encryption; AES-256 for data at rest. Private deployments can integrate with customer KMS/HSM.

Q: Can we bring our own keys?
A: Yes — we support external KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private, and optional BYOK for hosted Enterprise customers.

Q: How long do you retain logs and request data?
A: Default retention for request logs is 30 days; retention can be configured or disabled for Private deployments. Audit logs for Dedicated/Private are configurable per contract.

Q: Do you support compliance standards?
A: We have SOC 2 Type II in place; ISO and HIPAA support available via Private deployments and assessed on a per-customer basis. Ask for our compliance pack.

Q: What controls exist for model output safety and PII handling?
A: We provide content filters, prompt and response redaction hooks, and quality guardrails tied to eval frameworks. Customers can configure pre/post hooks and token-level redaction rules.

Q: How do you handle incident response and breach notifications?
A: Incidents are handled per our Incident Response playbook; critical breaches trigger our escalation path and customer notifications within contractually defined SLAs.

Appendices and assets (what to attach to proposals)
- Benchmarks: median & 99th tail latency graphs across model variants (hosted vs dedicated).
- Sample contract snippets: Dedicated SLOs and rollback clauses.
- Technical appendix: API examples (curl + SDK), quantization profiles, kernel optimizations summary.
- Sales assets: one-page competitive brief PDFs, slide deck template (.pptx), ROI calculator spreadsheet.

Operational notes for enablement admins
1) Keep price examples in this doc synchronized with Pricing team’s rate card (owner: Finance/Pricing).
2) Update competitor bullets quarterly (owner: Competitive Intelligence).
3) All pitch decks and case studies must route through Legal for quotes and customer names (owner: Legal + RevOps).
